query_hinglish: A 48-year-old man is being evaluated for an acquired defect of the myeloid stem cell line with a mutation in the PIG-A gene. His diagnosis was first suspected due to anemia and recurrent pink-tinged urine. Which of the markers will be negative in the flow cytometry test for his condition?

Rationale: The 48-year-old man's symptoms of anemia and recurrent pink-tinged urine alongside the mentioned PIG-A gene mutation suggest a diagnosis of Paroxysmal Nocturnal Hemoglobinuria (PNH). PNH is an acquired hematopoietic stem cell disorder characterized by the clonal expansion of cells that lack glycosylphosphatidylinositol (GPI) anchors due to the PIG-A mutation. CD55 (also known as Decay Accelerating Factor - DAF) and CD59 are GPI-anchored proteins that protect blood cells from complement-mediated lysis. Their absence on cells due to the PIG-A mutation leads to increased sensitivity to complement and thus to hemolytic anemia and hemoglobinuria. Thus, on flow cytometry testing, there will be a population of cells negative for CD55, which indicates PNH cells. Other markers such as CD19 (B cell marker), CD40L (T cell marker), and CD3 (pan T cell marker) are not GPI-anchored and are not affected by the PIG-A mutation, so they would not be expected to be negative in the case of PNH.

query_hinglish: If the genetic material were isolated and injected into the cytoplasm of a human cell, which of the following would produce viable, infectious virions?

Rationale: Rhinovirus, the cause of the common cold, is a non-enveloped, single-stranded RNA virus that can assemble and produce infectious virions in the cytoplasm. It does not require nuclear processes for replication, unlike influenza and other viruses with segmented genomes that need to access the host cell nucleus. Rabies and Lassa fever viruses are enveloped viruses whose assembly generally involves budding from the host cell membrane, which may need more complex host-cell interactions. Therefore, the isolated genetic material of rhinovirus has the highest likelihood of forming viable virions when directly injected into the cytoplasm.

query_hinglish: The balance between glycolysis and gluconeogenesis is regulated at several steps, and accumulation of one or more products/chemicals can either promote or inhibit one or more enzymes in either pathway. Rationale: Acetyl-CoA promotes gluconeogenesis by activating pyruvate carboxylase, an enzyme critical for the initial step of gluconeogenesis, which is the conversion of pyruvate to oxaloacetate. Acetyl-CoA serves as an allosteric activator for pyruvate carboxylase, thereby enhancing gluconeogenesis. In contrast, increased levels of AMP indicate a low energy state and would promote glycolysis to generate more ATP. Insulin is a hormone that stimulates glycolysis and inhibits gluconeogenesis. Fructose-2,6-biphosphate is a potent activator of phosphofructokinase (PFK-1, an enzyme in glycolysis) and an inhibitor of fructose-1,6-bisphosphatase (an enzyme in gluconeogenesis), thus it promotes glycolysis and suppresses gluconeogenesis.
